title: Screw four propellers onto a quadcopter's motors, each the way its motor's thread runs
instruction: Screw all four propellers down onto the quadcopter's motors until each hub sits tight on its motor bell, then let go.
context: Fitting propellers is the last step of every drone build and every crash repair, done by hobby builders, technicians who service inspection and survey drones, and teams that build robots to collect training data. On a quadcopter two motors spin clockwise and two anticlockwise, so their shaft threads run opposite ways and each prop tightens under its own motor's torque instead of working loose. A prop turned the way the other motors take only spins on the thread and, forced, strips it.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; the table top is at z 0.7475. (1) Quadcopter frame, 4-inch class: carbon-fibre cross arms 190 mm tip to tip, 12 mm wide and 4 mm thick, on a 36 x 36 x 16 mm electronics stack and a 50 x 50 x 6 mm base plate, matt black sRGB (0.12, 0.12, 0.14), 0.5 kg with battery, bolted to a 12 mm plywood bench plate that is clamped to the table (modelled fixed). Centre at (0.170, 0.000); arm tops 24 mm above the table. (2) Four motors, 24 mm diameter x 12 mm aluminium bells, 30 g each, bolted on the arm ends at (0.227, 0.057) front left, (0.113, 0.057) back left, (0.227, -0.057) front right, (0.113, -0.057) back right; bell tops 36 mm above the table. Front left and back right spin clockwise: red bells sRGB (0.80, 0.12, 0.12), M5 shaft thread cut left-hand. Front right and back left spin anticlockwise: blue bells sRGB (0.15, 0.30, 0.85), thread cut right-hand. The thread is a 3-start M5 form of 2 mm pitch (6 mm lead), 4 mm long, above the bell. (3) Four propellers, 4-inch (102 mm) two-blade, glass-filled nylon, 8 g each: a 16 x 16 x 14 mm square hub cap with a threaded bore, hub colour matching its motor (red for front left and back right, blue for front right and back left), and two blades 43 x 12 x 2 mm, dark grey sRGB (0.20, 0.20, 0.22), at the hub's foot. Hub friction 0.6 static / 0.5 dynamic. Each prop starts started on its motor's thread, hub foot 4 mm above the bell (hub centre 0.048 m above the table). The hub's thread is cut to match its own motor: turned the way the thread runs it advances 6 mm per turn and stops against the bell after 240 deg; turned the other way it only spins on a plain relief (about 400 deg), then jams. Verify before the trial: with a spare prop off the motor, turn it with the thread by hand and check it advances 1 mm per 60 deg and its foot reaches the bell after 240 deg; turn it against the thread and check it spins freely without moving. A thread gauge confirms 2 mm pitch, 3 starts and the hand on every shaft. Material and friction of the table are the station defaults.
scoring: Measured every control step from reset: each hub's drop below its starting height (4.0 mm = foot on the bell), and each hub's wrong-way turn (how far it has been turned against its own thread below its starting angle, in degrees). Whole-run record, cleared only by the simulator reset, so unscrewing and starting again never clears a wrong-way turn. Gate, any time in the run, gives 0: any one prop turned 180 deg or more against its thread (it is cross-threaded and ruined). Ladder, from the end state: 0.2 for each prop screwed down to within 0.4 mm of the bell (drop at least 3.6 mm), so 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 for one to four props; 1.0 when all four are tight and the release gate holds. Release gate: both grippers at least 30 mm from every prop and still (under 10 mm/s) for 1.0 s. Real-trial measurement: tight = a 0.4 mm feeler gauge does not enter between a hub's foot and its bell (check with the gauge at the end, after both hands are clear); wrong-way turn = a white paint dot on each hub cap read against the top camera frame by frame, summing every turn made against the thread's direction (180 deg is the dot reaching the opposite side); release = a ruler in the top frame shows 30 mm between each gripper and the nearest hub, and the gripper does not move for 1 s (30 frames at 30 fps).
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Unscrew every prop to its starting position: hub foot 4 mm above the bell (a 4 mm spacer under each hub, removed after), hub corners aligned to the arm directions. Check each shaft's thread hand and that a spare prop spins freely against the thread. Wipe the threads with a drop of light oil. Put a white dot on each hub cap. The frame and bench plate are clamped on taped outlines and need no reset.
fidelity: A 4-inch quad with rigid props. The thread is a software coupling (hub drops 6 mm per turn with the thread, stops at the bell) with a free-spin relief against it, not a modelled helix; the shaft and bore are not modelled. Props start 4 mm above the bell and the frame is fixed. Motors and frame are rigid and unpowered.
